title: Field-Gated Programming of Nested Skyrmion Bags by Spatially Selective Skyrmion Writing
abstract: Nested skyrmion bags are composite magnetic solitons whose internal occupation numbers provide an expanded state space for multilevel information encoding. However, deterministic and region-selective writing of individual skyrmions into nested bags remains challenging. Here, using micromagnetic simulations, we propose a field-gated nanocontact protocol for generating and programming double-layer nested skyrmion bags S(m,S(n)). The protocol exploits the opposite field responses of bag regions with antiparallel magnetic backgrounds. Spatially segmented perpendicular magnetic fields selectively expand either the outer region or the inner bag until it overlaps with a nanocontact. A spin-polarized current pulse of the appropriate polarity then nucleates one skyrmion in the selected region, while subsequent field-driven contraction moves the written skyrmion away from the contact and restores the writing site for repeated operation. Starting from an empty nested bag S(0,S(0)), this procedure enables the controlled construction of S(m,S(0)), S(0,S(n)), and general S(m,S(n)) states. The simulated total topological charge changes in unit steps during sequential writing, confirming one-at-a-time and region-selective control. These results provide a possible route toward programmable nested topological states for multilevel spintronic information encoding.
summary: This work proposes a novel field-gated protocol to program complex nested skyrmion bags $S(m, S(n))$ in magnetic thin films. By sequentially expanding and writing into the outer and inner regions using tailored perpendicular magnetic fields and current pulses, the authors achieve deterministic control over the total topological charge. This demonstrates a viable pathway for realizing multilevel spintronic memory elements.
main_problem: The challenge lies in achieving deterministic and region-selective writing of individual skyrmions into complex, nested magnetic structures called skyrmion bags $S(m, S(n))$ for advanced information encoding.
main_result: A field-gated nanocontact protocol was successfully simulated to demonstrate the controlled construction of arbitrary nested skyrmion bag states, confirming unit-step control over total topological charge.
method: The authors utilized micromagnetic simulations to model the dynamics, employing a three-stage cycle: selective magnetic field expansion (field gating), current-induced nucleation via spin-polarized pulses, and subsequent field-driven contraction.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using chiral ferromagnetic thin films (Co/Pt bilayer) containing nested skyrmion bags $S(m, S(n))$. The physics is governed by the micromagnetic energy functional and dynamics are described by the LLG equation with STT.
key_observables: Total topological charge ($Q_{	ext{total}} = n - m$), which changes in unit steps during writing; the size modulation of outer ($D_{	ext{out}}$) and inner ($D_{	ext{in}}$) bag diameters as functions of applied fields.
important_parameters: Material parameters include $M_s$, exchange stiffness ($A$), and DMI strength ($D$). Operational fields are set to $\pm 20 	ext{ mT}$ for stable expansion/contraction around a nanocontact.
main_assumptions: The protocol assumes precise control over spatially segmented perpendicular magnetic fields and the ability to apply highly localized, polarized current pulses.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the field-dependent size modulation of nested bags (Fig. 2) and demonstrate sequential writing protocols for constructing $S(m, S(n))$ states by showing the evolution of total topological charge over time (Figs. 3 & 5).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model using micromagnetics, details the field-gating mechanism via spatially segmented fields to define nested regions, and then presents a cyclical protocol combining field control with current pulses to achieve deterministic, region-selective writing of skyrmions.
why_interesting: While focused on spintronics, the precise, controlled manipulation of topological defects using external stimuli (fields/currents) mirrors concepts in controlling quantum states or excitations in engineered quantum systems.

Figure 4 shows representative magnetization configu- rations of double-layer nested skyrmion bags S(m, S(n)) with different values of m and n. Here, m denotes the number of skyrmions confined in the outer bag, while n denotes the number of skyrmions confined in the inner bag. The vertical and horizontal directions in the config- uration map therefore correspond to increasing m and n, respectively. Because the outer and inner bag regions have oppo- site background magnetizations, skyrmions written into these two regions contribute opposite unit topological charges.
